## Natural history notes

A small bee fly characterized by a fuzzy bee-like body, long legs, clear to lightly smoky wings, and a stiff forward-pointing proboscis used to drink nectar from flowers. In Florida, Systoechus solitus has been recorded from sandy natural areas such as Archbold Biological Station in Highlands County, and is most likely found in sunny scrub, sandhill, pine flatwoods, roadsides, and wildflower patches where adults visit blossoms. Adults feed on nectar and may act as pollinators, while the larvae of Systoechus bee flies are generally associated with grasshopper egg pods, making them part of the natural enemy community in open sandy habitats.
